<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: Small businesses are increasingly utilizing digital tools, including business software and cloud computing services, in their daily operations. Digital tools have been shown to improve small business job creation, revenue growth, and forecasting certainty.\1\ Among American small businesses that use digital tools in eight or more areas of operation, 67% report higher productivity, 45% report increased revenue, and 62% report predicating higher sales revenue in the future, outperforming businesses that use fewer digital tools in each reporting area.\2\ The Covid-19 pandemic accelerated the implementation of digital tools in small businesses and digital tools have become essential to businesses, supporting productivity and efficiency across all areas of operation.
\1\John Dearie, New Report Demonstrates Need for Small Business Technological Advancement Act, Ctr. for Am. Entrepreneurship (Feb. 18, 2025), https://startupsusa.org/new-report-demonstrates-need-for-the-small-business-technological-advancement-act.
\2\Intuit Quickbooks, Small Business Index Annual Report 2025: State of Small Business in the US, Canada, & the UK 115-118 (last visited Oct. 9, 2025).
Historically, loans from the Small Business Administration's (SBA) flagship 7(a) loan program have been available for use as working capital, including for the purchase and use of digital tools. However, many small businesses were unsure as to whether they could utilize 7(a) loans to finance digital tools. In June 2025, the SBA clarified that small businesses may use 7(a) loans to acquire and use business software or cloud computing services.\3\ Still, small businesses report remaining uncertain and say that cost is the most significant barrier to adopting the digital tools needed to remain competitive in the modern economy.\4\
\3\SOP 50.10.8: Lender and Development Company Loan Programs 50, U.S. Small Bus. Admin. (Jun. 1, 2025), https://www.sba.gov/document/ sop-50-10-lender-development-company-loan-programs.
\4\Intuit QuickBooks, supra note 2, at 120.
The Small Business Technological Act of 2025 would remove any uncertainty small businesses face and ensure that low-cost financing is available for the acquisition and use of digital tools. By codifying this provision, the bill affirms the ability of small businesses to use 7(a) loans to finance business software, cloud computing services, and other digital tools that support business operations, ensuring this remains consistent across different administrations. This codification will address concerns over the cost of digital tools and facilitate further integration of those tools into the operations of small businesses.
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
